rv.q: It pulls you irrepressibly in with its rousing message that life is not for regret but for kindness, gratitude – and most of all for living.
This most unlikely of musicals turns out to be real gem—hilariously funny, but also not missing the tragedies of life and how we deal with them.
Even more curiously, this was the narrative basis of what could well be one of the best new British musicals of recent years.

But although the first act feels twee and often baldly declamatory, with freshly introduced characters blurting out their innermost fears and feelings without provocation, the story gains momentum and emotional heft in a significantly tighter second half.Contunues...
“Flawless” isn’t an adjective I find cause to use very often in reviews.
It would "take a heart of Antarctic ice not to be moved by how this unravels".
A very clever combination of the powerful and the gentle which makes you feel just that little bit more hopeful for mankind at the end.

cn.t: Critics praise this life-affirming musical adaptation of Rachel Joyce's novel, celebrating its moving exploration of grief and hope, Mark Addy's performance, and Passenger's foot-stomping songs that elevate Harold's spiritual journey.

vr.q: Harold Fry is something truly magical.
